newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire government rejects rebel truce.
newsitem.headline: Zaire government rejects rebel truce.

text.p: Zaire said on Friday it did not recognise a ceasefire called by rebels holding a large slice of the country's eastern provinces.
Interior Minister Kamanda wa Kamanda told Reuters that Zaire saw neighbouring Rwanda as the aggressor in the east and Kinshasa would continue to do all in its power to recover its lost territory.

"We do not recognise this ceasefire. In this war we believe that the other side is the government of Rwanda and those who are supporting Rwanda so we shall do everything in our means to recover our territory," he said, speaking in English.
"As far as the government is concerned there are no negotiations to be envisaged with those who have attacked our country," he added.

Laurent Kabila, political leader of the Tutsi-led rebels in eastern Zaire declared a unilateral ceasefire on Thursday and urged the international community to push Zaire's government into negotiations.
He told Reuters that as part of the ceasefire the advancing rebels had stopped short of the towns of Walikale, west of Goma, and Bunia, north of Goma on the Ugandan border.
"We want them (Kinshasa) to negotiate instead of calling in friends and mercenaries," he said.
But Kamanda and government spokesman Boguo Makeli said that Zaire was intent on recapturing its territory before anything else could be considered.

"Sooner or later Zairean forces will be in a position to launch a counter-attack to recover the territory. There is no doubt about that," Kamanda said. "Zaire would not disregard assistance from friendly countries," he added.
A two-month offensive has seen the rebel coalition overwhelm Zaire's ragged army in the east, often without a fight.
The rebels now control a swathe of territory about 500 km (300 miles) long from north to south in eastern Zaire, including the main towns of Goma, Bukavu and Uvira.
